en: Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to ocean tides.
Taal Volcano features a unique nested structure with a crater lake located inside a larger lake on Luzon.
The Philippine Rise is a massive submerged volcanic plateau in the Pacific Ocean that is larger than Luzon.
Mount Hamiguitan hosts a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only a few meters tall due to ultramafic soil.
Mount Mayon in Albay is globally renowned for possessing the most perfectly symmetrical cone shape among all active volcanoes.
The Tamaraw, an endangered dwarf buffalo found exclusively on Mindoro, is smaller than a water buffalo and has V-shaped horns.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching 425 kilometers between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Mount Pulag, the highest peak in Luzon, is famous for its frequent sea of clouds phenomenon at its summit.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest known reserves of nickel, making it a top global producer.
Lake Mainit is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of 223 meters in Surigao.
The Philippines has the third longest coastline in the world, measuring approximately 36,289 kilometers of continuous marine boundaries.
